8.prediction: Use collect_prefix(u32) when a bounded prefix is a useful result; collect_all(NonZeroU32) only when completeness is required and a page-bound stop must error; pages(u32) for lazy per-page processing. A bound is not provider exhaustion. Prefix and lazy summaries should distinguish why traversal stopped and count delivered work; a zero prefix/page bound should send no requests. Exact summary field and enum names need verification.
8.answer: Choose collect_prefix(u32) for useful bounded partial results (Prefix<Item> with items and summary), collect_all(NonZeroU32) for required completeness (Vec only after PageStep::Done within the effective bound), and pages(u32) for lazy processing/search or deliberate application stop. Continued traversal at the bound produces PageBound/NextRequestKnown; collect_all returns Pagination/CompletionLimitExceeded with the summary rather than a success prefix. Done on the last allowed page is Exhausted without an extra request. Requested bound is intersected with runtime page ceiling. Zero prefix/pages does no shaping/controller/auth/quota/transport work and has PageBound/Unknown with no operation ID. Summary contains operation ID, stop reason, continuation, requested/effective bounds, received/delivered page and item counts, application attempts, replays, quota admissions, acquired bytes, identity bytes and aggregate dispatch knowledge, not a claim about items processed by application code. Apply controls before pages(); Pages lacks RequestControls. next_page() yields one error then Ok(None), so inspect the summary; finish() records Application unless already terminal. Dropping a started fetch cancels traversal; an unpolled dropped fetch does nothing.

9.prediction: Successfully awaiting a ByteStream or ItemStream endpoint means status/head validation and acquisition of a managed stream, not EOF/completion. Later reading can complete, fail or be cancelled; early drop cannot claim exhaustion/rollback. Unlike pagination, dropping a single pending stream-read future may retain resumable stream state; exact summary names and drop behavior require verification.
9.answer: Successful stream endpoint await validates the accepted head and opens a managed stream; operation completion and ApiResponse body disposition report StreamOpened, not completed download. Consumption later has Active/Eof/Application/Cancelled/Failed state in StreamSummary. Actual body completion and all records delivered establishes Eof; finish() before completion does not drain and records Application, preserving an existing terminal state. Dropping the handle early records Cancelled and releases native/decoder state. A terminal consumption error is delivered once, then next() returns None, while summary retains failure and original operation/attempt/status with ResponseObserved and FailureStage::StreamConsumption. Dropping only a pending next() future preserves stream state and resumes bounded acquisition later, without resend or resetting idle accounting. External cancellation cancels the whole stream. Finite total lease includes consumer pauses; idle counts pending-read time; byte/frame/record/time failures can occur after successful acquisition. No retry/auth recovery/native replay occurs after handoff. Acquisition metadata stays a snapshot, and stream summary supplies later facts.
